items.note: The page follows the paper's route: normalized cost table, margin list, justification of each row from the lemmas, setup and exceptional repair shown to be o(V), then the total O(Tp p^{1-kappa}) with a schoolbook cutoff. The closing paragraph explains that g_2 is the product of three small numbers epsilon, c, 1-tau, which is why the exponent is so close to one.

The table row 'Prefix moves | dK | epsilon(1+c) | g_1=1-epsilon(1+c)' follows from the stated sizes d=Theta(p^epsilon) and K=Theta(p^{epsilon c}). The bullet gives 'O(dK) linear scans, each O(V)', as the paper's Lemma does.

Row pK^{tau-1} with power 1-epsilon c(1-tau) follows from K=Theta(p^{epsilon c}). The bullet derives the cost, and the margin is evaluated as 'g_2=2^{-75}2^{-56}2^{-50}=2^{-181}', which the page identifies as the smallest.

Row ell d^{lambda'} with power 1-epsilon(1-lambda') follows from ell=Theta(p^{1-epsilon}) and d=Theta(p^epsilon). The bullet 'Each of at most ell rounds costs O(Vd^{lambda'})' gives the normalized cost, and g_3=2^{-75}2^{-54}=2^{-129} is computed.

g_2 and g_3 are computed as explicit products of the stated parameters. g_1>1/2 follows at once from epsilon=2^{-75}, at the paper's own level of 'direct substitution'.

With kappa=2^{-182} defined in the first line, 'the smallest margin is 2^{-181}=2 kappa' follows from the list. The slack role is stated later: 'any fixed power of log p is at most p^kappa eventually, which the margin 2 kappa leaves room for'.
The page applies the interchange lemma (linked as Fast address-chunk interchange) to width-K chunks: 'each costing O(VK^tau)'. The paper's argument is exactly this application of Lemma chunk-swap.
'The layout needs O(p/K) chunk exchanges, as d ell=O(p), ... The total is O(p/K)K^tau=O(pK^{tau-1})' reproduces the paper's count and product.

items.note: O(p) scans give O(V_call dp2^{-K}) per call. Summing over at most p^A visits of volume O(V), with d=O(p^epsilon), gives O(Vp^{O(1)}2^{-K})=o(V), which matches the paper's O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K}). The stated reason, 'K ... beats every power of p', is imprecise (recorded as a minor error).
'Each of the seven powers is at most 1-2 kappa' follows from the margin list and min g_i = 2 kappa, both shown above on the page.
'any fixed power of log p is at most p^kappa eventually' is asserted without argument, as in the paper. It is a standard asymptotic fact, but the page does not show it.

errors.quote: the repair costs $O(Vp^{O(1)}2^{-K})=o(V)$, because $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ beats every power of $p$
errors.problem: K = Theta(p^{epsilon c}) is far smaller than p, so K does not beat every power of p. What beats every power of p is 2^K, because K grows faster than log p. The paper says only 'Here d=O(p^epsilon) and K=Theta(p^{epsilon c}) with epsilon c>0', which is what makes p^{A'} 2^{-K} -> 0.

errors.quote: Each move peels one excess bit, exchanges the equal-width parts and restores it
errors.problem: In the paper the excess bit is peeled only 'when widths differ by one'; equal-width axes are exchanged directly. The page makes the peeling unconditional.

errors.quote: Let $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$ be the volume, the number of stored bits of $T$ coefficients of $p$ bits
errors.problem: The paper's coefficient formats use Theta(p) bits per coefficient, not exactly p, so the padded array has Theta(V) stored bits. V = Tp is the normaliser and equals the stored bit count only up to a constant.
